data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large service with high internal redundancy is more resilient because it eliminates the 'Coordination Gap' and 'Patch Latency' inherent in decentralized networks.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The centralized orchestrator itself becomes a single point of failure (SPOF) or a source of correlated crashes due to complexity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The redundancy is so high that the system can survive the loss of multiple internal zones without losing global availability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Decentralized networks suffer from asymmetric update speeds; a known vulnerability remains exploitable across the network for longer than in a centralized system.
